transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm... I don't know. I just came in because I can't seem to shake this heavy feeling. It's like... like everything I've tried to build since my divorce just collapsed, and I'm just sort of... stuck under it. It's just very hopeless right now.
How long has it been since your divorce?
Um... a while. I don't really... I try not to keep track of the exact date. Just a while.
How has this 'heavy feeling' been affecting your ability to handle your daily responsibilities, like work or taking care of your home?

Well... it's been pretty bad. At work, I... I was making some questionable calls. I kind of fell apart during a few meetings, which is... not great. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off all active project decisions. 

And at home... I don't know, I just stopped. I haven't been keeping up with any basic routines at all. It actually got to the point where... well, I ended up being sent to the emergency room recently. Because I just... I didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore.

When you look back at the last few months, do you feel that these intense feelings of hopelessness and your inability to function are exclusively tied to the events surrounding your divorce, or have you experienced these same feelings at other times in your life when things were otherwise stable?
I don't know... I mean, I guess I've felt down before. But... I don't really know if it was exactly like this. I haven't really thought about it.

When you are in these periods of feeling stuck, do you find that you are moving and speaking much more slowly than usual, or do you feel a sense of restlessness that makes it impossible for you to sit still?
I don't really know. I guess... I just don't do much of anything. I don't think I'm moving fast or slow, I just... I sit there. I don't really pay attention to how I'm moving.
Looking back over your entire life, can you recall any other periods, perhaps years ago, where you felt this same level of hopelessness and inability to function that lasted for at least two weeks?
I... I can't really remember. I mean, maybe? But... I don't think it was ever this bad. I just... it's hard to think back that far right now. I'm not sure.
Have you ever seen a doctor, therapist, or taken medication for these kinds of feelings at any point in the past?
No, I... I haven't. I've never gone to anyone for this. I just... I didn't think I needed to before.
During this current period, have you experienced any moments where you lost touch with reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others could not?
No. No, nothing like that. I haven't... I don't hear things.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep since you started feeling this way?

I... I haven't really paid attention to my appetite. But my sleep is... it's not good. I mostly just lie awake. Staring at the ceiling, replaying bills or... mistakes I've made at work. And if I do fall asleep, I wake up way before dawn. It just feels like I never actually slept.
During this time, have you found that you are unable to experience any pleasure at all, even from things you used to enjoy, or do you still find small moments of enjoyment?
I... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it. I guess I just... I don't feel much of anything right now.
When you are feeling your worst, do you find that your physical movements are so slowed down that other people have noticed it, or do you find yourself so agitated that you cannot stay still?
I don't know... I haven't really noticed. I just sit there, mostly. I don't think anyone has said anything.
Has anyone close to you mentioned that you seem to be moving or speaking significantly more slowly than you used to?
No... not that I know of. I haven't really been talking to anyone lately, anyway. So... no.

Have you found that your ability to think, focus, or make even simple decisions has become so impaired that you are having significant trouble managing basic daily tasks, like eating or dressing yourself?

I guess... it's hard to focus. I'll look at a basic drainage calculation for work, or a spreadsheet I've used for years, and... my mind just blanks. I just sit there rereading the same numbers. I can't really trust any decision I make. It's just... hard.
Are you able to physically take care of your basic hygiene, such as bathing, brushing your teeth, or dressing yourself, or have you stopped doing these things entirely?
I... I still get dressed. I mean, I put clothes on. I don't really shower as much as I should, I guess. But I'm not... I'm not completely stopping. Just... doing the bare minimum.
Has anyone told you that you look like you're moving or speaking in slow motion?
No. Like I said... I haven't really been around people enough for them to say anything.
Even when something good or positive happens, do you find that your mood does not brighten at all?
I don't know. Good things don't really happen right now. I just... I don't feel much of anything.
Have you noticed if your physical movements or your speech have become so noticeably slow or agitated that they have interfered with your ability to perform simple, routine physical tasks?
No... I don't think so. I can still do basic things fine... physically, at least. I just don't do them much.
